correctness.rationale: The finite root-of-unity identity makes each generator choose one cosine coefficient. Orthogonality fixes the exact \(L^2\) norm. Majority-support minimization gives the variational identity in both directions. Multinomial counts give the finite law; disjoint majority classes give the binomial atom. Strong-law counts, finite-union binomial tail sandwich and Stirling provide the sharp limit/exponent. A half-supported Fourier polynomial has exactly fair-Bernoulli lattice outputs and a persistent one-half median failure probability. The package checker performed 19584 independent finite assertions; the infinite statements have analytic arguments.

value.rationale: This is the complete sharp worst-case law on the naturally induced Fourier alias-slope subspace of the original median rank-one lattice estimator, not a chosen numerical tolerance slice. It resolves an explicit boundary of repeated generator randomization: a fixed smooth integrand has one-half failure probability for every odd number of repetitions, while the adaptive realized worst-case exhibits an explicit nonzero floor and a sharp stabilization exponent. This distinction between individual integrands and sampled worst-case functions is relevant for interpreting and stress-testing median-lattice guarantees.
